sense: a talk given to an audience

evidence: Cic. Brut. 91: scrībuntur ōrātiōnēs habitae jam
Traupman 176: ōrātiōnem habēre, give a speech
terms.comment: Ōrātiōnem habēre, to give a speech. Lewis & Short: “a set speech”, as against sermō, ordinary talk.

terms.gloss: a speech to a public meeting; the meeting itself
evidence: Cic. Fam. 9.14.7: lēgī enim contiōnem tuam
terms.comment: An address to the people or to an army, called together by a magistrate or a general.

terms.gloss: speak, make a speech (to a gathering)
terms.grammar: verbum, verbī n., with faciō, facere, fēcī, factum

phrases.latin: sed quid agō? paene ōrātiōnem in epistulam inclūsī.
phrases.english: But what am I doing? I’ve nearly put a whole speech into a letter.

phrases.latin: plēraeque enim scrībuntur ōrātiōnēs habitae jam, nōn ut habeantur
phrases.english: for most speeches are written down once they have been given, not in order to be given

sources: Lewis & Short: oratio · Lewis & Short: contio · Lewis & Short: verbum
